note: Rejudged 2026-10-17 after 7af5edbb7f. RFC 4456 Section 8 read in rfc/full/rfc4456.txt: "This attribute is 4 bytes long and it will be created by an RR in reflecting a route." The commit changed checkReflectorWithdrawal (both tags) only in its last failure: the Established re-check now returns interoplab.WithSearchedOutput(errors.New(...), output), which always returns a non-nil error wrapping the same cause (output.go). Every condition is byte-identical: the positive still requires the exact injector-log token 800904<3 octets>03 (flags 0x80, type 9, length 4, the client's identifier) beside the CLUSTER_LIST token, requireNoEarlyReflectorWithdrawal still refuses a withdrawal before FRR is asked, and the negative still requires the byte-exact withdrawal body :02:0004180A14000000 (withdrawn length 4, 10.20.0.0/24, Total Path Attribute Length 0), so no ORIGINATOR_ID rides the withdrawal. The unit covers TestReactorForwardRRInjects, TestReactorForwardRRPreservesOriginator and TestForwardReflectionLeavesAWithdrawalUntouched are unchanged and keep the 2026-10-06 judgement: absent originator becomes exactly four bytes 10.0.0.1, a present one stays byte-exact, withdrawal and EOR stay untouched with an advertisement control. The interop units carry no discrimination record and the scenario was not rerun for this failure-text change, so question 2 for them rests on reading; the unit tests carry the precise assertions. Verdict unchanged.
